title: Trailer
when: Launches, announcements, teasers and any film whose job is anticipation rather than explanation
rules: Three acts: a cold open (sketch signal), a rising montage of 2–4 s shots split by black type cards, a silence (sketch flatline), the title (sketch title), then a button.
Every montage shot is a place the promise touches, drawn for this film (wires, citygrid, mast are examples): never a stock skyline reused from another film.

Cards are flat, matte posters: a small lead line over one or two words (sketch card, sketchText LEAD and CARD). The main title outranks them: bigger, backlit, filling with metal (sketch title). No glow or aberration on type.
Cut clean: hard cuts on action between moving shots, one white flash at the title, never a smeared whip or a dissolve. Each montage shot is shorter than the last.
Compose the vertical cut for 9:16: stacked type within the middle 80% of the width, scenes staged tall (sketches get w and h).
